arcane.name: Arcane
arcane.identity: Remember a small committed outcome, then pay to echo its damage. Rune edits help mixed dice qualify while copied events remain distinct from physical actions.
arcane.loop: Play a sequence to earn Aether → record committed damage → pay for a bounded Echo → use Rune and Mirror to protect the next setup.
statuses: Persistent. After your second accepted card play in a round, gain 1 Aether, once per round. Copies and automatic triggers are not card plays. At Offensive reveal spend up to 2 Aether for +1 damage each to one own ability.

After an own non-copy ability or card damage source commits at least 1 actual damage, you may record its amount, capped at 3, and source ID. Choose one if several qualify together. Lasts until replaced or consumed. Never records status damage, Echo damage or a descendant of an Echo. Copies no statuses, costs, rolls or prevention.
Positive die overlay · own combat die · max 1

Choose one face. Until next Offensive exit that face adds Sigil alongside its original symbol for qualification, with no numeric change. Physical and face-set results can qualify; only physical rolls trigger other overlays.

During an application response, optionally consume Mirror to cancel one negative combatant-status stack against you and propose it against its enemy source controller in a child batch. New target and cap must be legal; otherwise the reflected application fails. Mark reflected so it cannot be reflected again. Expires after next Ongoing exit.
abilities: Gain 2 Aether and apply Rune to one own die face if absent.
Deal 5 damage. Optionally pay 2 Aether and consume an existing Echo Record at selection to queue its Echo after this attack.
Deal 6 damage and gain Mirror if absent. Optionally pay 1 Aether at selection to draw 1 afterward.
Each Sigil prevents 1; each Lens gains 1 Aether; any Star applies Rune to one own die face if absent.
Sigil: prevent 2. Lens: prevent 3. Star: prevent 2 and gain Mirror if absent.
cards: Apply Rune to one own combat die face if absent.
Pay 2 Aether and consume your Echo Record; Echo its recorded damage against one enemy.
Pay up to 2 Aether; add 2 damage each to one own damaging ability.
Pay 2 Aether; gain 1 Energy. Once per round.
Move your Rune to another owned die face, preserving original expiry.
Consume your Echo Record; prevent its recorded amount from one source instead of dealing Echo damage.
Pay 2 Aether and consume an existing Echo Record; queue its Echo after your selected ability. Requires unused Echo allowance.
Shift one unbound own combat face by 1 without wrapping; revalidate.
Reroll one revealed effect die belonging to any actor once. It resolves for its normal owner; overlays can trigger, but the roll is not copied.
Pay 1 Aether; set one own effect die to face 3, with no physical-roll triggers.
Pay 1 Aether; cancel one negative status stack proposed against you.
Prevent 2 from one source targeting you.
Pay Mirror; prevent 2 from one status source instead of reflecting an application.
Pay 1 Aether; remove one negative overlay from an owned die face or public own card.
After your first combat roll, set one unbound own combat die to face 4.
Consume Echo Record; gain 1 Aether and draw 1.
Upgrade once per battle: your second-card Aether reward grants 2 instead of 1.
Pay 2 Aether; prevent 4 and gain Mirror if absent after commit.
Pay 3 Aether; restore 1 eligible own damage-removed card to discard and apply Rune if absent.
pairs: swarm
The same second accepted card play can earn Aether and Brood. Echoed outcomes never count as a third card or a fresh play.
fortune
Rune and Boon can share a face. A set face may qualify through Rune but cannot manufacture Favor from Boon.
curse
Double Refraction can reroll an enemy status die carrying Curse, adding another physical overlay opportunity. Echo copies a damage number and never replays that roll or its Curse overlays.
flame
Flame’s direct attacks can fill an Echo Record after actual damage. Echo cannot reapply Burn or copy a Kindling status source.
arcane.example: Prism Bolt actually deals 2 after defense, so record 2. Next round Minor Echo pays 1 Energy, 2 Aether and the record to deal 2 card damage. It opens damage responses but cannot write another record or replay Poison attached to the original attack.
arcane.counter: Prevent direct damage to deny good records. An Echo tops out at 3 and consumes its record. Mirror does not reflect die overlays, costs, positive statuses or already reflected applications.
arcane.balance: All Echo creation shares one per controller per round, reserved at acceptance without refund. Echo is ordinary card damage, not an extra ability; it has the copied tag and original-source ancestry for loop checks.
combos: Prism Bolt → Echo Record → Minor Echo
Record actual damage after defense, capped at 3. Minor Echo consumes that record and two Aether to replay only the number, not statuses, rolls or on-play rewards.
Inscribe → Lens Shift → mixed qualification
Put Rune on face 4 of a partner die, then set that die to 4 after rolling. It retains its original symbol and adds Sigil, but neither Boon nor Curse physically triggers.

beast.name: Beast
beast.identity: Study a rival’s repeated choices, mark a quarry, and choose when to pounce. Tracking uses public ability history, never private dice or hands.
beast.loop: Name a Quarry → observe a repeat or punish marked prey → earn Instinct → spend it on a precise strike or a bounded follow-up.
statuses: Persistent. At shared Offensive reveal, gain 1 if your Quarry selected the same nonempty ability ID as in its previous Offensive segment; once per round. Initial encounters, passed turns and different tiers of the same ID are handled explicitly: no prior ID means no reward, tier changes still repeat.
Negative · enemy · cap 1 per Beast controller

One living enemy may be your Quarry. Applying it to another removes your prior Quarry; markers from other controllers are independent. Persistent. Once per round at Offensive reveal, pay 1 Instinct for +2 damage to your ability targeting your Quarry.

At Offensive reveal, optionally consume up to 2 on that enemy for +1 ability damage each. A committed damaging status batch against your Quarry applies 1 Scent, once per round per controller, even if another type supplied the status. Expires after next Defensive exit.

After your next non-copy Offensive ability removes at least one enemy health card, consume Pounce to create one 1-damage follow-up against the same enemy. Ordinary card damage; no new defense, always damage responses. At most one follow-up per controller per round; expires after the following round’s Damage Resolution exit.
abilities: Choose a Quarry and gain 2 Instinct.
Deal 5 damage; gain Pounce if absent. Newly gained Pounce waits for a later attack, not this one.
Deal 6 damage. Optionally pay up to 2 Instinct at selection for +1 damage each; apply Quarry if you have none.
Each Claw prevents 1; each Track gains 1 Instinct; any Tooth applies 1 Scent to the attacker.
Claw: prevent 2. Track: prevent 3. Tooth: prevent 2 and gain Pounce if absent.
cards: Apply Quarry to one enemy; once per round.
Apply 1 Scent to your Quarry and draw 1. Requires a living Quarry.
Pay up to 2 Instinct; add 2 damage each to one own ability targeting your Quarry.
Pay 2 Instinct; gain 1 Energy. Once per round.
Pay 1 Instinct; apply 2 Scent to your Quarry.
Pay 1 Instinct; grant +1 damage to each of up to two existing own sources targeting your Quarry.
Remove your existing Quarry; gain 1 Instinct. No enemy means no reward.
Prevent 2 from one incoming ability source.
Pay 1 Instinct; prevent 3 from one source targeting you.
Shift one unbound enemy combat face by 1 without wrapping; revalidate.
Reroll one own revealed effect die once.
If your Quarry has at least one unreleased damage-removal proposal, pay 1 Instinct to gain Pounce for a later qualifying attack.
Pay 1 Instinct; cleanse 1 own negative status stack.
Cancel one proposed Quarry or Scent stack against you; gain 1 Instinct only if canceled.
Pay Pounce; prevent 2 from one source. You forgo that follow-up.
If your Quarry is attacking you, pay 1 Instinct; prevent 2 and apply 1 Scent after defense resolves.
Upgrade once per battle: your first repeat-ability Instinct reward each round grants 2 instead of 1.
Pay 2 Instinct and 2 enemy Scent; add 4 damage to your chosen ability against that enemy. It must be your Quarry.
Pay 2 Instinct; draw 2 and gain Pounce if absent. Does not increase the follow-up allowance.
pairs: venom
Quarry takes actual Poison damage → Scent is applied once. Spend Scent on a later direct attack; many Poison dice never generate many Scent in the same round.
frost
Frostbind narrows easy rerolls, making repeated ability choices more likely. Beast reads the actual public choice, not a presumed forced choice.
swarm
Pack Signal can improve two existing Swarm sources. Extra small sources do not each trigger Pounce because it listens only to a non-copy Offensive ability.
beast.example: The Quarry repeats Needlefang at a new tier: gain one Instinct because the ability ID repeated. An earlier Poison batch gave it Scent. Pay one Instinct through Quarry and consume one Scent for +3 on one attack.
beast.counter: Vary ability IDs to deny repeat rewards. Cleanse Scent before reveal. Stop every card removal from the main attack to deny Pounce; overage alone is not a hit.
beast.balance: Instinct has no automatic generic damage spend beyond the explicit Quarry option. Pounce has a one-per-round shared allowance and cannot retrigger itself or other follow-up listeners.
combos: Choose the Trail → repeated enemy ability → Lunge
Instinct rewards a real repeat of the Quarry’s ability ID. Lunge converts the reserve into damage; changing targets to chase it gives up the old Quarry.
Crouch → Raking Claws → Pounce
Gain Pounce before attacking. If Claws actually removes a health card, Pounce deals its single follow-up. The new Scent can strengthen a later attack but does not retroactively improve Claws.

blood.name: Blood
blood.identity: Choose exactly when to pay health cards for power. Bleed pressures the enemy while Blood Marks turn committed injury into a limited supply.
blood.loop: Apply a Blood Mark → cause real damage → gain Ichor → spend it on attack or recovery; Sacrifice is an optional, explicit shortcut.
statuses: Persistent. When you voluntarily Sacrifice an eligible own hand or discard card, gain 2 Ichor in a child batch, maximum once per round. At Offensive reveal spend up to 2 Ichor for +1 damage each to one own ability. Sacrifice is never automatic.

Use the active game rule: each Ongoing entry deals 1 status damage per captured stack, then removes one stack total. It does not roll a die. With no interference, 1/2/3 stacks deal 1/3/6 lifetime damage.

After at least one health card is removed from this target by damage, consume 1 Blood Mark to grant its applier 1 Ichor. Maximum one per target per batch. Prevented damage, overage, and Sacrifice do not qualify. Expires after next Damage Resolution exit.
Spend 1 during a damage response to prevent 2 from one status source targeting you. Persistent. Does not prevent Sacrifice.
abilities: 4 / 5 / 6 damage and apply 1 Blood Mark to that enemy after damage commits. This new Mark does not count that same damage.
Gain 2 Ichor and 1 Clot. No health payment.
Deal 4 damage and apply 1 Bleed. Optionally pay 1 Ichor at selection to apply one additional Bleed.
Deal 6 damage. Optionally pay 2 Ichor at selection: if this attack removes at least 1 enemy health card, restore 1 eligible own damage-removed card afterward.
Each Fang prevents 1; each Vein gains 1 Ichor; any Chalice gains 1 Clot.
Fang: prevent 2. Vein: prevent 3. Chalice: prevent 2 and apply 1 Blood Mark to the attacker.
cards: Apply 1 Blood Mark to one enemy.
Sacrifice one additional eligible own hand or discard card; draw 1. Native Ichor reward remains capped once per round.
Pay up to 2 Ichor; add 2 damage each to your selected damaging ability.
Pay 1 Ichor; apply 1 Bleed and 1 Blood Mark to one enemy.
Pay 2 Ichor; gain 1 Energy. Once per round.
Pay 2 Ichor; restore 1 eligible own damage-removed card to discard.
Pay 1 enemy Bleed; add 2 damage to your selected ability against that enemy.
Prevent 2 from one source targeting you.
Sacrifice one additional eligible own card not currently threatened; prevent 4. Payment cannot be prevented or restored.
Pay 2 Ichor; redirect 1 damage from a source targeting you to its enemy controller.
Set one unbound own combat die to face 1 or 4; revalidate.
Reroll one own revealed effect die once. No reward based on the discarded face.
Pay 1 Ichor; cleanse 1 own negative status stack.
Remove 1 own Bleed; gain 1 Clot. Requires Bleed.
Pay 1 Ichor; cancel one negative status stack proposed against you.
Choose one threatened own card. If damage removes it, gain 1 Ichor and 1 Clot after commit.
Upgrade once per battle: the first Blood Mark you consume each round grants 2 Ichor instead of 1.
Pay 3 Ichor; prevent 4. If at least 1 damage still removes your health cards, restore 1 eligible prior damage removal after this batch.
Pay 3 Ichor; restore 2 eligible own damage-removed cards to discard. Once per battle; never revives a finally defeated actor.
pairs: venom
Poison damage can consume an existing Blood Mark and generate Ichor; a single batch still spends only one Mark even with several toxin sources.
grave
Sacrifice creates a Corpse record for Grave’s information/resource engine, but the paid card is never eligible for restoration. This prevents refunded sacrifices.
stone
Armor handles enemy attacks so you can afford voluntary Sacrifice. Sacrifice cannot be reduced by Armor or counted as prevention.
verdant
Regrowth and Blood restoration share a cap. Spores reward actual Bleed application; Bleed’s larger lifetime total makes repeated stacks a deliberate investment.
blood.example: An enemy with a Blood Mark loses two cards to Poison: consume one Mark, gain one Ichor. Paying that Ichor later increases an ability; it does not create more Blood Marks unless a card or ability says so.
blood.counter: Prevent all real health-card removal to deny Marks. Cleanse Bleed early, before its stacked lifetime damage grows. Pressure the Blood player after it pays an unpreventable Sacrifice.
blood.balance: Sacrifice removes a chosen additional own hand/discard card at acceptance, records it as paid, and requires at least 2 remaining health cards before payment. It is not damage and cannot use a card already committed to removal or this played card. Bleed is deterministic, unlike Poison.
combos: Blood Seal → partner Poison damage → Crimson Edge
An existing Blood Mark earns Ichor from actual enemy card loss. Crimson Edge spends it for attack damage; preventing all Poison damage denies the Mark reward.
Bloodletting → Grave Corpse conversion → Borrowed Pulse
Sacrifice can fund Ichor and an optional Grave record, but Borrowed Pulse may only restore a different, damage-removed card. The paid sacrifice stays paid.

construct.name: Construct
construct.identity: Install a small public machine, then select which program runs. Reusing the same resource-spend and prevention events creates synergy without manufacturing unlimited parts.
construct.loop: Gain Scrap → install a Module → choose one program each round → spend resources or prevent damage to run it → repair or salvage deliberately.
statuses: Persistent. Once per round after an own installed Module is dismantled as an explicit cost or destroyed by an enemy effect, gain 1 Scrap after the event. Expiry/replacement is not destruction. At Action timing, pay 2 Scrap to install one missing Module; once per round.
Positive installed objects · self · max 2 distinct

Choose Ram, Recycler or Plating; one of each maximum. At Offensive entry choose one installed Module as active until round end. Ram: first own ability source finalized gains +1 damage. Recycler: first explicit spend of another positive status grants 1 Scrap after commit; Scrap spending excluded. Plating: first incoming damage batch may prevent 1 from one source. Each active program runs once per round. Installed objects persist; no separate turns or HP.

At Defensive reaction, optionally consume 1 to reduce one chosen enemy defense’s prevention by 2, minimum zero. Maximum one per target per round. Expires at next Defensive exit. Cards and resource prevention are unaffected.
Positive die overlay · own combat die · max 1

Name one number when installed. Until next Offensive exit, once in your planning after a roll, you may clear Calibration to set that unbound die to the named face. No physical-roll triggers; normal revalidation.
abilities: Gain 2 Scrap and install one missing Module if a slot exists. This install uses the round’s one-install allowance.
Deal 4 damage and apply 2 Corrosion. Optionally pay 1 Scrap at selection for +2 damage.
Deal 6 damage. Optionally dismantle one installed Module at selection for +3 damage; its active program is unavailable afterward.
Each Gear prevents 1; each Rivet gains 1 Scrap; any Core applies Calibration to one own combat die if absent.
Gear: prevent 2. Rivet: prevent 3. Core: prevent 2 and apply 1 Corrosion to the attacker.
cards: Install one missing Module with an open slot; use the shared once-per-round install allowance.
Apply Calibration to one own combat die, naming face 1 or 4.
Pay up to 2 Scrap; add 2 damage each to one own damaging ability.
Dismantle one installed Module; gain 1 Energy. Its native Scrap reward is limited once per round.
Pay 1 Scrap; replace one installed Module with a missing one. Uses install allowance; no destruction reward.
Switch active Module to another installed one. Does not reset any module’s once-per-round usage.
Pay 2 Scrap; restore 1 eligible own damage-removed card to discard.
Pay 1 Scrap; prevent 3 from one source.
Pay 1 Scrap; cancel one negative status stack proposed against you.
Shift one unbound own combat face by 1 without wrapping; revalidate.
Reroll one own revealed effect die once; does not reset any module.
Remove 1 existing Corrosion from yourself; gain 1 Scrap. Requires Corrosion.
Pay 1 Scrap; reduce prevention from one enemy defense by 2, minimum zero.
Dismantle one own Module; prevent 4. Native salvage reward can occur once per round.
Move existing Calibration to another own die, keeping its named face and original expiry.
Upgrade once per battle: your first Module destruction reward each round grants 2 Scrap instead of 1.
Pay 2 Scrap; gain 1 Armor and install one missing Module if allowed. No slot means Armor only.
Pay 3 Scrap; halve one source after source prevention, rounding down, before damage-reaction prevention.
pairs: storm
Recycler can gain Scrap when Charge is explicitly spent. The returned Scrap is not Charge and cannot retrigger the same program.
tide
Flow spending can run Recycler. Plating’s actual prevention can earn Flow, but each program and Flow reward has its own once-per-round latch.
stone
Module Plating and Armor combine. Corrosion and Fracture reduce selected defense prevention with a floor of zero; excess reductions are lost.
fortune
Calibration can complete an ability on a Boon face, but setting it does not roll it or earn Favor. Fortune rerolls can instead chase both outcomes.
construct.example: Activate Recycler, then spend one Flow on prevention. After the spend commits, gain one Scrap. Spending more Flow this round gives no extra Scrap. Rewire and Change Program never reset Recycler’s latch.
construct.counter: Pressure resources before an installation turn. Corrosion expires and cannot defeat late card prevention. Only one Module is active at a time; removal sacrifices its program.
construct.balance: All installs, including ability/card installs, share one per controller per round. New modules become selectable next Offensive entry unless Change Program explicitly switches. Programs never run retroactively.
combos: Assembly Kit → active Recycler → partner resource spend
Install Recycler, activate it at the next Offensive entry, then spend Flow/Charge/another positive status. Gain Scrap once. Change Program cannot reset that used program.
Spare Stock → Acid Wash → Core Hammer
Corrosion reduces a selected defense; Core Hammer can dismantle a Module for burst. Dismantling loses the program and only returns the capped salvage reward afterward.

flame.name: Flame
flame.identity: Turn short-lived burns and card embers into a controlled burst. Heat rewards status pressure even when another type supplied it.
flame.loop: Establish Burn → earn Heat from status damage → choose an early detonation or a stronger attack → bank Embers on cards that will cycle.
statuses: Persistent. After a batch commits at least 1 enemy status damage, gain 1 Heat; once per round, regardless of source type or stack count. At Offensive reveal, optionally spend up to 2 for +1 damage each to one own Offensive ability source. No source means no payment.

At next Ongoing entry capture existing stacks. They create one status-damage source of 1 per stack; captured stacks expire when outcomes finalize, even if damage is prevented. Applications during that entry wait for the next one.

After the next enemy-targeting status-damage source is collected, consume 1 to add 1 to that source before its damage responses. Maximum one Kindling consumption per target per batch. Expires after the target’s next Ongoing exit.
Positive card overlay · own discard · max 2 marked cards

Choose a public own discard card. Until end of the following round, its next accepted play or committed damage removal grants 1 Heat in a child batch, then clears the overlay. Ordinary draws/discards do not trigger. No duplicate overlay on one card.
abilities: 4 / 5 / 6 damage and apply 1 Burn at every tier.
Gain 2 Heat and mark one own discard card with Ember, if available.
Deal 4 damage. Optionally pay up to 2 enemy Burn at selection for +2 damage each; consumed Burn will not tick.
Deal 6 damage and apply 1 Kindling. Optionally pay 2 Heat at selection to apply 2 Burn as well.
Each Spark prevents 1; each Coal gains 1 Heat; any Crown applies 1 Burn to the attacker (maximum 1 from this defense).
Spark: prevent 2. Coal: prevent 3. Crown: prevent 2 and apply 1 Kindling to the attacker.
cards: Mark one own discard card with Ember; requires an unmarked eligible card.
Draw 1. If you already have Heat, mark one eligible own discard card with Ember.
Pay 1 enemy Burn; create 2 ordinary card damage against that enemy.
Pay up to 2 Heat; add 2 damage per stack to your selected damaging Offensive ability.
Discard one additional hand card; gain 2 Heat. The discarded card can carry Ember but discarding does not trigger it.
Draw 2, then discard 1. Apply Ember to the discarded card if an overlay slot is open.
Prevent 2 from an incoming status source. After commit gain 1 Heat if this prevented at least 1.
Pay 2 Heat; gain 1 Energy and draw 1. Once per round.
Prevent 3 from one incoming source; pay 1 Heat as an additional cost.
Pay 1 Heat; your chosen ability source ignores up to 2 source prevention, not damage reactions.
Set one own combat die to face 1 or 4; revalidate your selected ability.
Physically reroll one own revealed effect die once; resolve its final face normally.
Prevent 1. If actual prevention is positive, apply 1 Burn to that source’s enemy controller after commit.
Remove 1 own Burn to gain 1 Heat. Requires that Burn.
Pay 1 Heat; cancel one negative status stack proposed against you. Other stacks remain.
If you have no Heat, gain 1 Heat. Once per round.
Apply 1 Burn and 1 Kindling to the same enemy as separate proposals.
Upgrade once per battle: the first Ember trigger you resolve each round also draws 1 card.
Pay 2 Heat; prevent 5 from one source. No retaliation or new Heat from this card.
Pay 3 Heat; apply 3 Burn divided among legal enemies, maximum 2 per enemy. With one enemy apply only 2.
pairs: venom
Poison and Volatile damage can earn Heat and spend Kindling. Neither effect adds toxin checks or interferes with Catalyst.
grave
A damage-removed Ember card can create both its Heat reward and a Grave Corpse; one shared removal event, two bounded listeners.
stone
Afterglow can prevent 2 status damage and earn its Heat reward plus Stone’s Resolve in the same batch. Both rewards require actual prevention; neither is granted per point prevented.
flame.example: With 1 Kindling and 2 Poison on the enemy, a Poison damage batch consumes one Kindling for +1 total damage. If any status damage commits, gain exactly 1 Heat, not one per stack. Next round spend that Heat on an ability.
flame.counter: Cleanse Burn before its entry; it expires even if prevented. Deny Heat by preventing every status-damage source in a batch. Force Heat spending before the burst.
flame.balance: Burn is worth at most 1 delayed damage per newly applied stack, unlike Poison’s unmodified expected lifetime 2. Cinderlash starts at 5/6/7 total before prevention. Flashpoint trades two future points for four immediate, defendable points.
combos: Dry Tinder → First Spark → Flashpoint

Kindling is setup for a later status source; Flashpoint may consume Burn for immediate damage instead. Choosing that detonation gives up Burn’s scheduled point, so Kindling may need a partner’s Poison/Web source.
Pocket Ember → Burning Lesson → Ember Ledger
Mark a discard card, cycle toward it, then gain Heat when that card is actually played or damage-removed. The upgrade adds a draw only on the first successful Ember trigger each round.

fortune.name: Fortune
fortune.identity: Put a temporary reward on a risky face, earn Favor from real rolls, and cash a capped streak. Luck is a choice of risk rather than unlimited corrections.
fortune.loop: Place Boon on a die face → physically chase it → earn Favor and a limited Streak → spend before the next risk or bank a Jackpot.
statuses: Persistent. A physical result landing on one of your Boon faces grants 1 Favor, at most twice per round across all your Boons and dice. Gain belongs to the die owner. No reward from face-setting, copied results or qualification inspection. At Offensive reveal spend up to 2 for +1 ability damage each.
Positive die-face overlay · own dice · max 2 marked faces total

Choose a currently unmarked face on an owned persistent combat die; at most one Boon per face. It adds a beneficial Fortune marker, not a combat qualification symbol. Lasts through next Offensive exit or two physical hits on that face, whichever comes first. It can coexist with Curse; both resolve from the same physical result.

After a voluntary combat reroll command hits at least one Boon, gain 1 Streak; if it hits none, remove 1 Streak. Once per command, not per die. Initial/forced/effect rolls neither raise nor lower Streak. At Action timing pay 3 Streak for Jackpot: gain 1 Energy and draw 2; once per round. Persistent otherwise.
At damage response, optionally spend 1 Insurance to prevent 1 from one source. If it actually prevents at least 1, gain 1 Favor after commit, maximum one such Favor reward per round. Persistent.
abilities: Apply one Boon if a slot exists; gain 1 Insurance.
Deal 5 damage. Optionally pay 1 Favor at selection to gain 1 Streak after commit.
Deal 6 damage; apply one Boon if a slot exists and gain 1 Favor. No literal seven-face die is required.
Each Pip prevents 1; each Coin gains 1 Favor; any Star gains 1 Insurance.
Pip: prevent 2. Coin: prevent 3. Star: prevent 2 and apply one Boon if a slot exists.
cards: Apply one Boon to a chosen own combat die face if a slot exists.
Apply one Boon to a face that already has Curse, or apply an ordinary Boon if no such own face exists.
Pay 1 Favor; roll one own persistent combat die as an effect. On 1–3 gain 1 Insurance; on 4–6 gain 1 Streak.
Pay up to 2 Favor; add 2 damage each to one own damaging ability.
Pay 2 Favor; gain 1 Energy. Once per round.
Pay 2 Streak; draw 2 and gain 1 Insurance. Does not count as Jackpot.
Move one own Boon to an unmarked face of the same die, preserving remaining hits and expiry.
Shift one unbound own combat face by 1 without wrapping; revalidate. Boon does not trigger.
Pay 1 Favor; physically reroll one own revealed effect die once. Normal overlays resolve on that roll.
Pay 1 Favor; set one own effect die to face 3. No physical-roll rewards.
Prevent 2 from one source targeting you.
Pay 1 Insurance; prevent 2 from one source instead of its usual 1. Native Insurance reward remains once per round.
Pay 1 Favor; cancel one negative status stack proposed against you.
Remove one own Boon; gain 1 Favor. Its remaining potential is lost.
After your first combat roll, set one unbound own combat die to face 4. No Streak or Favor trigger.
Pay 1 Streak; prevent 3 from one incoming ability source.
Upgrade once per battle: the first physical Boon hit each round grants 2 Favor instead of 1; still uses one of two reward slots.
Pay 2 Favor; gain 2 Streak and 1 Insurance. Normal caps apply; no automatic Jackpot.
Pay 3 Favor; prevent 4 and gain 1 Insurance after the batch commits.
pairs: curse
One face can hold both Boon and Curse. A physical hit grants bounded Favor and uncapped Curse Count; copied or face-set results grant neither.
storm

Voluntary rerolls can earn Charge and change Streak. An incoming Pulse can hit your Boon for Favor, but your outgoing Pulse rolls an enemy die and cannot grant you that enemy’s Favor. Pulse never changes Streak.
arcane
Rune can make a Boon face useful for an ability while Echo cannot replay Boon rewards. Moves preserve each overlay’s own duration.
radiant
Purify Face can remove Curse while keeping Boon. Insurance’s prevention can support defensive builds without counting as a cleanse.
fortune.example: Reroll three dice and hit two Boons. Gain at most two Favor and exactly one Streak. Reroll again with no Boon hit: lose one Streak. Any Curse overlays on those physical results still add their normal Curse Count.
fortune.counter: Force resource spending before a big payoff. Boons expire, have only two hits, and can occupy only two faces. Streak can fall when a voluntary reroll misses.
fortune.balance: No Fortune effect rerolls a die indefinitely or counts face-setting as a roll. Jackpot consumes all three Streak and uses its once-per-round allowance; gaining new Streak does not automatically cash it out.
hooks: H-10 physical roll and command grouping
combos: Good Omen → voluntary reroll → Bank the Run
Reroll toward the marked physical face. A hit can grant Favor and Streak; a miss lowers Streak. Cash two Streak safely or risk another command to reach Jackpot’s three.
Safety Net → Covered Loss → Raise the Stakes
Spend Insurance on actual prevention to earn its once-per-round Favor reward. Raise the Stakes converts stored Favor into damage; zero prevention earns no rebate.

frost.name: Frost
frost.identity: Make future decisions costly without skipping turns: one die can become fixed, one public card can become unavailable, and brittle targets crack under a chosen hit.
frost.loop: Apply Chill or Frostbind → keep a stable pool to gain Rime → choose control or direct pressure → spend Brittle on a decisive source.
statuses: At the target’s next Offensive entry, consume Chill and reduce its maximum roll commands by 1, minimum 1. Does not cancel an already accepted command. No refresh; extra-roll bonuses combine before the minimum/maximum clamps.
Negative die overlay · enemy combat die · max 1 per target

Mark a declared enemy combat die. During its next Offensive segment, it rolls in the initial pool, then cannot be voluntarily rerolled or face-set by either player. Forced rolls explicitly naming it remain legal. Clear at that segment’s exit. Never affects effect-roll requests.

Persistent. At your final Offensive reveal, gain 1 if at least two dice were kept through every voluntary reroll after the first roll; once per round. With no voluntary reroll, any two final dice qualify. Spend 1 in damage response to prevent 1.

At Offensive reveal, optionally consume up to 2 on your chosen enemy to add +1 each to one ability damage source. A consumed stack is lost if the source is later canceled. Expires after target’s next Defensive exit.
abilities: Gain 2 Rime and apply 1 Chill to one enemy.
Deal 5 damage; Frostbind one chosen enemy combat die for its next Offensive segment.
Deal 6 damage and apply 2 Brittle. Optionally pay 2 Rime at selection to also apply Chill.
Each Shard prevents 1; each Rime gains 1 Rime status; any Crystal applies 1 Brittle to the attacker.
Shard: prevent 2. Rime: prevent 3. Crystal: prevent 2 and gain 1 Rime.
cards: Apply Chill to one enemy if absent.
Frostbind one chosen enemy combat die if that enemy has no Frostbind.
Pay up to 2 Rime; add 2 damage per stack to your selected damaging ability.
Pay 2 Rime; gain 1 Energy. Once per round.
Pay 1 Rime; defer one existing own Burn or Bleed stack’s next Ongoing trigger by one entry. Each stack can be deferred once.

Pay 1 Rime; shift one unbound enemy combat face by 1 without wrapping and revalidate.

Keeping dice earns Rime while Armor handles incoming damage. Both reward committing to a stable plan, and Brittle adds pressure without extra rolls.

Chill slows the enemy’s attack setup while Poison matures. Preserve can delay your own harmful Bleed/Burn, but cannot postpone enemy Poison to preserve it indefinitely.

Frostbind can make the enemy retain a predictable die, supporting Scent tracking; it does not force an ability choice.
frost.example: A target with Chill and Overload enters Offensive: normal 3 commands +1 −1 =3. Frostbind allows its initial die roll, then locks that die for voluntary edits only. The target still selects any legal ability.
frost.counter: Cleanse control before Offensive entry. Keep a good Frostbound face and build around it. Frost cannot erase the initial roll, and its seals do not prevent health removal.
frost.balance: Ice Seal is a negative overlay on one publicly revealed enemy card, maximum one sealed card per target. Until end of next round the card cannot be played or voluntarily moved from discard to hand; normal draws, discards, reshuffle and damage removal remain legal. It never reveals a hidden hand. If the card is removed, clear the seal.

Frostbind fixes one enemy die after its initial roll next segment; Chill reduces the total command budget. A Beast partner can observe the enemy’s resulting public ability rather than guessing hidden dice.
Glaze → Breaking Point or native Brittle spend
Choose between spending Brittle for direct attack bonuses or paying two for 3 card damage. The latter costs an additional stack and card but can create a separate source.

grave.name: Grave
grave.identity: Record what was actually lost, harvest its remains, and haunt public cards as they move. Recovery preserves card identity and cannot refund costs.
grave.loop: Damage or sacrifice creates a Corpse record → consume it for Remnant → attach Haunt or recover an eligible card → keep one finite last-chance option.
statuses: When an own card is permanently removed by damage or Sacrifice, optionally create one linked Corpse; maximum 2 records per round, ignoring overage. At cap choose which old record to discard. Consuming a record does not move the physical card. Restore immediately deletes its linked record. Played/exhausted cards create no Corpse.
Persistent. At Action timing once per round, consume 1 Corpse to gain 2 Remnant. At Offensive reveal pay up to 2 Remnant for +1 damage each to one own ability.
Negative card overlay · enemy public card · max 2 per applier

Mark an enemy discard card or publicly revealed health card. Its next accepted play or committed damage removal creates 1 ordinary status damage against its owner, then clears Haunt. Maximum one Haunt trigger per applier per batch. Lasts through end of following round. It never reveals cards in hand/deck or triggers on ordinary discard.

Once per battle, after a damage batch leaves you pending defeat, you may consume Anchor and 2 Remnant to restore 1 eligible prior damage-removed card before final defeat. Requires an eligible card and remaining shared restore allowance. No eligible card means no payment. Expires only on use/removal; cannot save a finally defeated actor.
abilities: Gain 2 Remnant. Optionally consume 1 Corpse at selection to draw 1 after resolution.
Deal 4 damage; Haunt one eligible public enemy card if available. Optionally pay 1 Remnant for +1 damage at selection.
Deal 6 damage. Optionally consume 1 Corpse and pay 2 Remnant at selection to restore 1 eligible own damage-removed card after the attack.

Pay 2 Remnant; prevent 3 and gain Death Anchor if absent and unused. A subsequent rescue still costs 2 Remnant.

Sacrifice yields a paid-card Corpse usable for Remnant, but Unearth can only restore cards removed by damage. This is a resource trade, never a refunded sacrifice.

An Ember-marked own card can give Heat and a Corpse when damage removes it. Haunt damage against an enemy can earn Flame Heat.
verdant
Regrowth restores physical card instances and deletes their linked Corpse. A consumed Corpse cannot be spent twice, even if that card is damaged again later.

A Grave/Radiant creature has multiple rescue tools but shares restoration limits and only one last-chance rescue per battle.
grave.example: You sacrifice a hand card: it may make a Corpse and Ichor. Later consume that Corpse for Remnant. The card remains paid and ineligible for Restore; you may instead restore a different card lost to enemy damage.
grave.counter: Cleanse Haunt before playing the marked card. Deny damage removals or force corpse spending on defense. Exhaustion never generates Corpses.

radiant.name: Radiant
radiant.identity: Prevent new corruption, cleanse existing harm, and restore a small number of real lost cards. Protection and recovery have different timing and costs.

stone.name: Stone
stone.identity: Store real prevention, expose defensive weaknesses, and resist die manipulation. The damage you stop becomes a limited resource rather than a permanent immunity.
stone.loop: Raise Armor → prevent a meaningful hit → gain Resolve → spend on a counterattack or Fortify → use Fracture against protected enemies.
statuses: Persistent. During a damage response, spend up to 2 Armor to prevent 1 each from one source targeting you. No automatic consumption.
Persistent. After you actually prevent at least 2 damage in one batch, gain 1 Resolve, once per round. At Offensive reveal spend up to 2 for +1 ability damage each.

During Defensive reaction, consume up to 2 to reduce the prevention granted by one of that enemy’s selected defenses by 1 each, minimum zero. Does not reduce card prevention, scaling or unspent Armor. Expires at next Defensive exit.

Until your next Offensive exit, cancel the first enemy-proposed nonphysical edit to one of your combat dice, then consume. Does not stop rerolls, Curse overlays, or effects on status dice. Optional decline leaves Fortify unused.

storm.name: Storm

pairs: venom
Spores reward Poison stacks that actually fit, or a committed Incubation/Volatile application. Rejected Poison overflow alone is not a successful stack application.
blood
Blood can use Growth defense to survive its costs. Regrowth restores prior damage removals, never the cards paid as Sacrifice.
fortune
Graft and Boon may share a physical face. One adds a qualification symbol, the other rewards a physical roll; face-setting activates only the former.
grave
A restored card keeps its instance identity. Clear its old Corpse link so Grave cannot spend a stale corpse after revival.
verdant.example: Spores are on an enemy with 2 Poison. Twin Puncture adds one Poison and overflows one: the committed Poison gain consumes one Spore and earns Growth. Incubation’s later child application can consume another Spore if one remains.
verdant.counter: Force Growth spending before Income to break passive growth. Cleanse Spores before a partner application. Restoring a card to discard does not immediately draw it.
verdant.balance: Growth regeneration consumes both setup and 2 resource per restored card. Restoration is capped across mixed types and excludes sacrificed/exhausted cards. Extra Growth at cap is lost.
combos: Planting → Sleeping Root → Root Mend
Leave at least one Growth through Income to grow the reserve. Root Mend provides earlier repair, while Regrowth waits for Ongoing and pays its own two Growth. Both share restoration slots.
Spore Dust → partner status application → Bramble Burst
A successful new negative stack consumes one Spore for Growth. Spend that Growth through Bramble Burst, or preserve it to keep Income growth active.
